ticket.name: Deutschland-Ticket (regional)
ticket.excluded: ICE, IC and EC trains are not covered. The plan never puts you on one.

days.title: Into the Karwendel
days.intro: You arrive in the afternoon. One small alpine town, two lakes, and the Karwendel wall going pink at sunset.

paths.name: Town and lakes
paths.why: Gentle. No trains after you arrive.

seq.stn: Station to Obermarkt: 5 min on the flat.

paths.name: Hop into Austria
paths.why: One easy 20-minute ride over the border and back.

seq.stn: Station to Obermarkt: 5 min on the flat.

seq.note: Crosses into Austria. Your German ticket does not cover this stretch — buy the short Mittenwald–Seefeld ticket at the machine.

seq.stn: Station sits at the edge of the centre, 5 min in.

days.title: Alps to Augsburg
days.intro: Out of the mountains by way of an abbey and a village of painted houses.

paths.name: Abbey and woodcarvers
paths.why: The best of the route. Four short stops, none rushed.

seq.stn: Station to Ludwigstraße: 10 min.

seq.note: Bus 9606 from outside Garmisch station — it runs straight through to Ettal and on to Oberammergau.

seq.stn: The bus stops at the abbey gate.
Centre to station: 10 min.
Station to Obermarkt: 10 min.
Hbf to Rathausplatz: 15 min, or tram 2.

paths.name: Füssen and Neuschwanstein
paths.why: One big sight instead of four small ones. Early start, long day.

seq.note: Regional bus 9606 via Ettal and Oberammergau. Only a few runs a day — check the time the night before.

seq.stn: Station is beside the old town.
Hbf to Rathausplatz: 15 min, or tram 2.

days.title: Munich day
days.intro: Bags stay in Augsburg. A whole day in Munich and back for the night.

paths.name: Munich all day
paths.why: Most time in the city. Simplest day of the trip.

seq.stn: Hbf to Marienplatz: S-Bahn 5 min, or 20 min on foot.

paths.name: Landsberg, then Munich
paths.why: A quiet riverside town first, Munich from lunchtime.

seq.stn: Station is across the river, 10 min in.
Hbf to Marienplatz: S-Bahn 5 min.

paths.name: Augsburg day, Munich night
paths.why: Augsburg deserves more than an evening. Munich lit up after dark.

seq.stn: Hbf to Fuggerei: 20 min, or tram 1.
Hbf to Marienplatz: S-Bahn 5 min.

days.title: On to Nuremberg
days.intro: Two hours north, then a walled city with a castle on the rock above it.

paths.name: Nuremberg all day
paths.why: Arrive by 11 and have the whole city. Easiest on the legs.

seq.stn: Check out and walk to the Hbf.
Hbf to the old town: 5 min through the Königstor.

paths.name: Donauwörth on the way
paths.why: Breaks the ride with a pretty gabled street.

seq.stn: Station to Reichsstraße: 10 min.
Hbf to the old town: 5 min.

paths.name: Plus Bamberg in the evening
paths.why: Bamberg after dark is the prettiest thing on this stretch. A long day.

seq.stn: Drop the bags at the hotel first.
Station to the old town: 20 min, or bus 901.

days.title: Würzburg and Rothenburg
days.holiday: German Unity Day — a public holiday. Trains run to the Sunday timetable and museums may keep holiday hours.
days.intro: The longest day of riding, and two of the best towns in Germany.

paths.name: Würzburg first
paths.why: Palace in the morning light, Rothenburg in the afternoon.

seq.stn: Hbf to the Residence: 15 min.
Station to the Rödertor: 10 min.

seq.note: Two or three changes. Buy something to eat before you board.

seq.stn: Hbf to the Altstadt: 15 min by bus 33 or tram 5.
see: Marktplatz and Church of the Holy Spirit

paths.name: Rothenburg first, less riding
paths.why: Shorter total time on trains, and you reach Heidelberg an hour earlier.

seq.stn: Station to the Rödertor: 10 min.
Hbf to the Residence: 15 min.
Hbf to the Altstadt: 15 min by bus 33 or tram 5.

days.title: Heidelberg to Erfurt
days.intro: A castle in the morning and a bridge full of houses by dusk.

paths.name: Castle morning, Fulda stop
paths.why: You still get Heidelberg properly. Fulda breaks the ride.

seq.stn: Altstadt to Hbf: 15 min by bus or tram. Collect the bags first.
see: Marktplatz and Church of the Holy Spirit

seq.stn: Station to the cathedral: 15 min.
Station to the Krämerbrücke: 15 min.

paths.name: Wartburg Castle
paths.why: The single best castle on the route — but it costs you Heidelberg's morning.

seq.note: Very early start. Changes at Frankfurt, Fulda and Bebra.

seq.stn: Wartburg: bus 10 from the station, then a short climb — or 45 min uphill on foot.
Station to the Krämerbrücke: 15 min.

days.title: Erfurt to Berlin
days.intro: The last day. Two or three small stops on the way, and your brother at the end of it.

paths.name: Weimar and Naumburg
paths.why: Two short, beautiful stops. Very little walking between them.

seq.stn: Domplatz to the station: 10 min by tram 3 or 4.
Station to the centre: 15 min downhill.
Station to the cathedral: 15 min, or the historic tram.

seq.note: One or two changes, usually at Halle.

seq.stn: You have arrived. Berlin Hbf.

paths.name: Harz: Quedlinburg and Magdeburg
paths.why: Quedlinburg is the most complete half-timbered town in Germany. More changes, though.

seq.note: Two or three changes. Worth checking the night before.

seq.stn: Station to the Marktplatz: 10 min.
Hbf to the cathedral: 15 min.
You have arrived. Berlin Hbf.

oberau.name: Bahnhof Oberau
oberau.photoFile: Luftbild- Film 54 Bildnr. 81 - LABW - Staatsarchiv Ludwigsburg EL 68 IX Nr 13553.jpg

rothenburg.name: Bahnhof Rothenburg ob der Tauber
rothenburg.photoFile: Altstadt, von Südwesten Rothenburg ob der Tauber 20230518 0273.jpg

wurzburg.name: Würzburg Hauptbahnhof
wurzburg.photoFile: Würzburg, Festung Marienberg, Blick auf die Altstadt -- 2018 -- 0317-22.jpg

quedlinburg.name: Bahnhof Quedlinburg
quedlinburg.photoFile: Quedlinburg asv2018-10 img04 pano from Muenzenberg.jpg

mittenwald/Obermarkt.name: Obermarkt
mittenwald/Obermarkt.note: The painted main street — Lüftlmalerei on nearly every facade.

mittenwald/St Peter and Paul.name: St Peter and Paul
mittenwald/St Peter and Paul.note: Baroque church with a painted tower you can see from the whole valley.

mittenwald/Violin Making Museum.name: Violin Making Museum
mittenwald/Violin Making Museum.note: Mittenwald has made violins since 1684. Small, and genuinely lovely.

mittenwald/Lautersee.name: Lautersee
mittenwald/Lautersee.note: Mountain lake above the town. About 1 h up through the forest.

mittenwald/Ferchensee.name: Ferchensee
mittenwald/Ferchensee.note: The quieter second lake, 30 min further on from Lautersee.

mittenwald/Karwendel cable car.name: Karwendel cable car
mittenwald/Karwendel cable car.note: Up to 2244 m. A viewing platform over the whole range.

mittenwald/Leutaschklamm.name: Leutaschklamm
mittenwald/Leutaschklamm.note: Gorge walkway on steel catwalks over the water. 4 km from town.

mittenwald/Isar source valley.name: Isar source valley
mittenwald/Isar source valley.note: The Isar starts here and runs north to Munich.

seefeld/Seefeld centre.name: Seefeld centre
seefeld/Seefeld centre.note: Tyrolean pedestrian streets, cafés, mountain air.

seefeld/Wildsee.name: Wildsee
seefeld/Wildsee.note: Lake walk at the southern edge of the centre, flat and easy.

seefeld/Pfarrkirche St Oswald.name: Pfarrkirche St Oswald
seefeld/Pfarrkirche St Oswald.note: Late-Gothic church, the reason pilgrims came here.

seefeld/Seekirchl.name: Seekirchl
seefeld/Seekirchl.note: The little round white chapel on the meadow — Seefeld's postcard.

garmisch/Ludwigstraße.name: Ludwigstraße
garmisch/Ludwigstraße.note: Partenkirchen's old painted street. Prettier than the Garmisch half.

garmisch/Old St Martin.name: Old St Martin
garmisch/Old St Martin.note: Medieval frescoes inside, including a giant St Christopher.

garmisch/Partnachklamm.name: Partnachklamm
garmisch/Partnachklamm.note: Gorge cut 80 m deep. Walkway through the spray. 20 min walk to the entrance.

garmisch/Zugspitze.name: Zugspitze
garmisch/Zugspitze.note: Germany's highest point, 2962 m. Cog railway plus cable car. Half a day.

garmisch/Olympic ski stadium.name: Olympic ski stadium
garmisch/Olympic ski stadium.note: The 1936 jump. You can walk up to the top of the tower.
garmisch/Olympic ski stadium.about: Olympiaschanze was a ski jumping venue in St. Moritz, Switzerland, it was built in 1926 and closed in 2006.

garmisch/Eibsee.name: Eibsee
garmisch/Eibsee.note: Turquoise lake under the Zugspitze. A flat 7 km loop.

ettal/Ettal Abbey church.name: Ettal Abbey church
ettal/Ettal Abbey church.note: Benedictine abbey from 1330. The dome fresco is the thing to look up at.

ettal/Abbey shop and distillery.name: Abbey shop and distillery
ettal/Abbey shop and distillery.note: The monks' liqueur, beer and cheese, sold at the gate.

ettal/Schloss Linderhof.name: Schloss Linderhof
ettal/Schloss Linderhof.note: Ludwig II's small palace with the golden bedroom. Bus from Ettal.

oberammergau/Pilatushaus.name: Pilatushaus
oberammergau/Pilatushaus.note: The most famous painted facade in Bavaria — painted architecture that isn't there.

oberammergau/Passion Play Theatre.name: Passion Play Theatre
oberammergau/Passion Play Theatre.note: The village has staged the Passion every ten years since 1634.

oberammergau/Woodcarving workshops.name: Woodcarving workshops
oberammergau/Woodcarving workshops.note: Along Dorfstraße. Carvers still work in the windows.

oberammergau/Ettaler Straße houses.name: Ettaler Straße houses
oberammergau/Ettaler Straße houses.note: Hansel and Gretel and Little Red Riding Hood, painted across whole walls.
oberammergau/Ettaler Straße houses.about: Lüftlmalerei is a form of mural art that is native to villages and towns of southern Germany and Austria, especially in Upper Bavaria and in the Tyrol.

oberammergau/Pfarrkirche St Peter und Pa.name: Pfarrkirche St Peter und Paul
oberammergau/Pfarrkirche St Peter und Pa.note: Rococo interior, considered one of the finest village churches in Bavaria.

oberammergau/Laber cable car.name: Laber cable car
oberammergau/Laber cable car.note: Ten minutes up for the view back over the painted village.

murnau/Obermarkt.name: Obermarkt
murnau/Obermarkt.note: A colourful main street the Blaue Reiter painters put on canvas.

murnau/Münter House.name: Münter House
murnau/Münter House.note: Where Kandinsky and Gabriele Münter lived and painted. Still furnished.

murnau/Staffelsee.name: Staffelsee
murnau/Staffelsee.note: Lake with seven islands, 20 min walk from the centre.

murnau/Murnauer Moos.name: Murnauer Moos
murnau/Murnauer Moos.note: The largest intact moor in central Europe. Boardwalk trails.

murnau/Schlossmuseum Murnau.name: Schlossmuseum Murnau
murnau/Schlossmuseum Murnau.note: Blaue Reiter paintings in the old castle.

fussen/Neuschwanstein.name: Neuschwanstein
fussen/Neuschwanstein.note: Ludwig II's castle. Interior needs a timed ticket booked ahead.

fussen/Marienbrücke.name: Marienbrücke
fussen/Marienbrücke.note: The bridge over the gorge with the castle view everyone knows.

fussen/Hohenschwangau.name: Hohenschwangau
fussen/Hohenschwangau.note: The yellow castle below — where Ludwig actually grew up.

fussen/Hohes Schloss.name: Hohes Schloss
fussen/Hohes Schloss.note: Painted castle courtyard — trompe-l'œil windows on flat walls.

fussen/Füssen old town.name: Füssen old town
fussen/Füssen old town.note: Lanes of pastel houses right beside the station.

fussen/Lechfall.name: Lechfall
fussen/Lechfall.note: Waterfall and gorge, 10 min from the centre.

fussen/St Mang's Abbey.name: St Mang's Abbey
fussen/St Mang's Abbey.note: Baroque abbey on the river with a painted Hall of Princes.

munich/Marienplatz.name: Marienplatz
munich/Marienplatz.note: The heart of the city. Glockenspiel at 11:00 and 12:00.
munich/Marienplatz.about: Marienplatz is a central square in the city centre of Munich, Germany. It has been the city's main square since 1158.

munich/St Peter's tower.name: St Peter's tower
munich/St Peter's tower.note: 306 steps. The best view in Munich, straight down onto Marienplatz.

munich/Viktualienmarkt.name: Viktualienmarkt
munich/Viktualienmarkt.note: Open-air food market since 1807. Lunch here.

munich/Frauenkirche.name: Frauenkirche
munich/Frauenkirche.note: The two onion domes on the skyline. Free to enter.

munich/Residenz.name: Residenz
munich/Residenz.note: The Wittelsbach palace. The Antiquarium hall alone is worth it.

munich/Hofgarten.name: Hofgarten
munich/Hofgarten.note: Quiet formal garden behind the Residenz.

munich/English Garden.name: English Garden
munich/English Garden.note: Bigger than Central Park. Surfers on the Eisbach at the south end.

munich/Chinesischer Turm.name: Chinesischer Turm
munich/Chinesischer Turm.note: Beer garden under a wooden pagoda, in the middle of the park.

munich/Hofbräuhaus.name: Hofbräuhaus
munich/Hofbräuhaus.note: The famous beer hall. Loud, touristy, still fun once.

munich/Asamkirche.name: Asamkirche
munich/Asamkirche.note: A tiny baroque church squeezed between shops. Astonishing inside.

munich/Nymphenburg Palace.name: Nymphenburg Palace
munich/Nymphenburg Palace.note: Summer palace and park, 20 min by tram.

munich/Deutsches Museum.name: Deutsches Museum
munich/Deutsches Museum.note: The largest science and technology museum in the world.

munich/Oktoberfest.name: Oktoberfest
munich/Oktoberfest.note: On the Theresienwiese. In 2026 it runs to 4 October — expect big crowds.

augsburg/Rathausplatz.name: Rathausplatz
augsburg/Rathausplatz.note: Renaissance town hall and the Perlachturm above it.

augsburg/Golden Hall.name: Golden Hall
augsburg/Golden Hall.note: Inside the town hall. Gold leaf across the whole ceiling.

augsburg/Fuggerei.name: Fuggerei
augsburg/Fuggerei.note: Social housing founded in 1521. Rent is still 0.88 € a year. People live here.

augsburg/Maximilianstraße.name: Maximilianstraße
augsburg/Maximilianstraße.note: The grand street, with the Hercules and Mercury fountains.

augsburg/Augsburg Cathedral.name: Augsburg Cathedral
augsburg/Augsburg Cathedral.note: Has some of the oldest stained glass in the world, around 1100.

augsburg/Lechviertel canals.name: Lechviertel canals
augsburg/Lechviertel canals.note: The old craftsmen's quarter, threaded with water channels.

augsburg/St Ulrich and St Afra.name: St Ulrich and St Afra
augsburg/St Ulrich and St Afra.note: Two churches, Catholic and Protestant, sharing one building.

augsburg/Schaezlerpalais.name: Schaezlerpalais
augsburg/Schaezlerpalais.note: Rococo ballroom and a good picture gallery.

augsburg/Augsburg water management.name: Augsburg water management
augsburg/Augsburg water management.note: UNESCO-listed: 800 years of waterworks, towers and canals.

landsberg/Lech weir.name: Lech weir
landsberg/Lech weir.note: A stepped waterfall right in the middle of town.

landsberg/Hauptplatz.name: Hauptplatz
landsberg/Hauptplatz.note: Sloping square with the Schmalzturm and a painted town hall.

landsberg/Bayertor.name: Bayertor
landsberg/Bayertor.note: 1425 gate tower, climbable, 15 min uphill from the square.

donauworth/Reichsstraße.name: Reichsstraße
donauworth/Reichsstraße.note: A wide street of tall gabled houses, one of the best in Swabia.

donauworth/Ried island.name: Ried island
donauworth/Ried island.note: Where the Wörnitz runs into the Danube.

donauworth/Liebfrauenmünster.name: Liebfrauenmünster
donauworth/Liebfrauenmünster.note: Late-Gothic brick minster with the town's big bell.

donauworth/Käthe Kruse Doll Museum.name: Käthe Kruse Doll Museum
donauworth/Käthe Kruse Doll Museum.note: In an old monastery. Charming and odd.

nuremberg/Imperial Castle.name: Imperial Castle
nuremberg/Imperial Castle.note: Walls, a very deep well, and the roofs of the old town below.

nuremberg/Hauptmarkt.name: Hauptmarkt
nuremberg/Hauptmarkt.note: The Schöner Brunnen fountain — turn the brass ring for luck.

nuremberg/Albrecht Dürer's House.name: Albrecht Dürer's House
nuremberg/Albrecht Dürer's House.note: Where Dürer lived and worked, below the castle.

nuremberg/Weißgerbergasse.name: Weißgerbergasse
nuremberg/Weißgerbergasse.note: The prettiest surviving half-timbered lane in the city.

nuremberg/Henkersteg.name: Henkersteg
nuremberg/Henkersteg.note: Covered wooden bridge over the Pegnitz, with the hangman's house.

nuremberg/Frauenkirche.name: Frauenkirche
nuremberg/Frauenkirche.note: On the market square. The clock figures move at noon.

nuremberg/St Lorenz.name: St Lorenz
nuremberg/St Lorenz.note: Huge Gothic church with Veit Stoß's Annunciation hanging in the choir.

nuremberg/Germanisches Nationalmuseum.name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum
nuremberg/Germanisches Nationalmuseum.note: The biggest museum of German culture. Enormous.

nuremberg/Documentation Centre.name: Documentation Centre
nuremberg/Documentation Centre.note: The Nazi rally grounds, honestly explained. 15 min by tram.

nuremberg/Nuremberg sausages.name: Nuremberg sausages
nuremberg/Nuremberg sausages.note: Three in a roll, or a dozen on a pewter plate at Bratwursthäusle.

nuremberg/Handwerkerhof.name: Handwerkerhof
nuremberg/Handwerkerhof.note: Craft courtyard inside the wall by the station. Touristy but pretty.

bamberg/Old Town Hall.name: Old Town Hall
bamberg/Old Town Hall.note: Built on an artificial island in the middle of the river, painted all over.

bamberg/Little Venice.name: Little Venice
bamberg/Little Venice.note: Fishermen's houses leaning over the water.

bamberg/Bamberg Cathedral.name: Bamberg Cathedral
bamberg/Bamberg Cathedral.note: Four towers, and the Bamberg Horseman inside.

bamberg/Schlenkerla.name: Schlenkerla
bamberg/Schlenkerla.note: Smoked beer, poured from the barrel. Tastes like bacon. Try it once.

bamberg/New Residence rose garden.name: New Residence rose garden
bamberg/New Residence rose garden.note: Terrace garden with the best view over the roofs.

bamberg/Michaelsberg Abbey.name: Michaelsberg Abbey
bamberg/Michaelsberg Abbey.note: On the hill above, with a ceiling painted with 600 medicinal plants.

rothenburg/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
rothenburg/Marktplatz.note: Town hall tower is climbable — narrow stairs, big reward.

rothenburg/Plönlein.name: Plönlein
rothenburg/Plönlein.note: The crooked yellow house between two gates. The photo everyone takes.

rothenburg/Town wall walk.name: Town wall walk
rothenburg/Town wall walk.note: Covered walkway along the top. The east side is the best stretch.

rothenburg/Burggarten.name: Burggarten
rothenburg/Burggarten.note: Castle garden at the western end, looking down the Tauber valley.
rothenburg/Burggarten.photoFile: Skulpturen im Burggarten Rothenburg ob der Tauber 20231030 0047.jpg

rothenburg/St Jakob's.name: St Jakob's
rothenburg/St Jakob's.note: Riemenschneider's Holy Blood Altar, carved in limewood around 1500.
rothenburg/St Jakob's.about: St. James Church is a Gothic church in Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Germany.

rothenburg/Medieval Crime Museum.name: Medieval Crime Museum
rothenburg/Medieval Crime Museum.note: Six hundred years of law and punishment. Grim and fascinating.

rothenburg/Käthe Wohlfahrt.name: Käthe Wohlfahrt
rothenburg/Käthe Wohlfahrt.note: Christmas, all year, in a shop the size of a village.

wurzburg/Würzburg Residence.name: Würzburg Residence
wurzburg/Würzburg Residence.note: UNESCO. Tiepolo's staircase fresco is the largest in the world.

wurzburg/Old Main Bridge.name: Old Main Bridge
wurzburg/Old Main Bridge.note: Stone saints along the parapet. People drink wine on it at sunset.

wurzburg/Marienberg Fortress.name: Marienberg Fortress
wurzburg/Marienberg Fortress.note: 30 min climb through the vineyards, or bus 9. The view is the point.

wurzburg/Würzburg Cathedral.name: Würzburg Cathedral
wurzburg/Würzburg Cathedral.note: One of the largest Romanesque churches in Germany.

wurzburg/Marktplatz and Marienkapelle.name: Marktplatz and Marienkapelle
wurzburg/Marktplatz and Marienkapelle.note: Red-and-white Gothic chapel on the market square.

wurzburg/Court Garden.name: Court Garden
wurzburg/Court Garden.note: Behind the Residence, free to walk into.

wurzburg/Franconian wine.name: Franconian wine
wurzburg/Franconian wine.note: Dry white in the flat round Bocksbeutel bottle. Local to here.

heidelberg/Heidelberg Castle.name: Heidelberg Castle
heidelberg/Heidelberg Castle.note: Red sandstone ruin above the town. Funicular from Kornmarkt.

heidelberg/Philosophers' Walk.name: Philosophers' Walk
heidelberg/Philosophers' Walk.note: Across the river and up. The classic view back at the castle.

heidelberg/Old Bridge.name: Old Bridge
heidelberg/Old Bridge.note: 1788. The bronze monkey at the end is for holding, and for luck.

heidelberg/Hauptstraße.name: Hauptstraße
heidelberg/Hauptstraße.note: 1.6 km of pedestrian street, the longest in Germany.

heidelberg/Marktplatz and Church of the.name: Marktplatz and Church of the Holy Spirit
heidelberg/Marktplatz and Church of the.note: Market square church with shops built into its outer walls.

heidelberg/Student Prison.name: Student Prison
heidelberg/Student Prison.note: Where misbehaving students were locked up — and covered the walls in graffiti.

heidelberg/Königstuhl funicular.name: Königstuhl funicular
heidelberg/Königstuhl funicular.note: Continue past the castle to the top of the hill.

fulda/Fulda Cathedral.name: Fulda Cathedral
fulda/Fulda Cathedral.note: Baroque, over the tomb of St Boniface.

fulda/St Michael's.name: St Michael's
fulda/St Michael's.note: 9th century, one of the oldest churches in Germany, right beside the cathedral.

fulda/City Palace.name: City Palace
fulda/City Palace.note: Prince-abbots' palace, with a mirror cabinet.

fulda/Palace gardens and Orangery.name: Palace gardens and Orangery
fulda/Palace gardens and Orangery.note: Free to walk through, with the huge Floravase at the top.

eisenach/Wartburg.name: Wartburg
eisenach/Wartburg.note: UNESCO castle where Luther translated the New Testament in ten weeks.

eisenach/Bach House.name: Bach House
eisenach/Bach House.note: Bach was born in Eisenach. Live demonstrations on historic instruments.

eisenach/Market square.name: Market square
eisenach/Market square.note: Town hall, the Georgenkirche where Bach was baptised, and cafés.
eisenach/Market square.photoFile: Thuringia Eisenach asv2020-07 img28 Market Square.jpg

eisenach/Luther House.name: Luther House
eisenach/Luther House.note: Where Luther lodged as a schoolboy.

erfurt/Krämerbrücke.name: Krämerbrücke
erfurt/Krämerbrücke.note: A bridge with houses on it, lived in continuously since 1325.

erfurt/Domplatz.name: Domplatz
erfurt/Domplatz.note: Cathedral and St Severi side by side above a huge open square.

erfurt/Erfurt Cathedral.name: Erfurt Cathedral
erfurt/Erfurt Cathedral.note: Climb the steps. The Gloriosa bell inside is the largest medieval bell in the world.

erfurt/Petersberg Citadel.name: Petersberg Citadel
erfurt/Petersberg Citadel.note: Baroque fortress on the hill. Best place for sunset over the city.

erfurt/Fischmarkt.name: Fischmarkt
erfurt/Fischmarkt.note: Renaissance houses and the town hall. Dinner here.

erfurt/Augustinian Monastery.name: Augustinian Monastery
erfurt/Augustinian Monastery.note: Luther was a monk here for six years.

erfurt/Old Synagogue.name: Old Synagogue
erfurt/Old Synagogue.note: The oldest standing synagogue in Europe, with a hoard of medieval treasure.

erfurt/egapark.name: egapark
erfurt/egapark.note: Big garden park on the edge of town, if you want green.

weimar/Goethe's House.name: Goethe's House
weimar/Goethe's House.note: On Frauenplan. He lived here for fifty years; it is exactly as he left it.

weimar/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
weimar/Marktplatz.note: Town hall and the Cranach house, with the old Elephant hotel.

weimar/Park an der Ilm.name: Park an der Ilm
weimar/Park an der Ilm.note: Landscape park along the river, with Goethe's garden house in it.

weimar/Bauhaus Museum.name: Bauhaus Museum
weimar/Bauhaus Museum.note: The Bauhaus started in this town in 1919.

weimar/Duchess Anna Amalia Library.name: Duchess Anna Amalia Library
weimar/Duchess Anna Amalia Library.note: The oval rococo hall. Timed tickets, limited numbers, book ahead.

weimar/Theaterplatz.name: Theaterplatz
weimar/Theaterplatz.note: The Goethe and Schiller statue stands in front of the theatre.

naumburg/Naumburg Cathedral.name: Naumburg Cathedral
naumburg/Naumburg Cathedral.note: UNESCO. The twelve founder statues — Uta especially — are extraordinary.

naumburg/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
naumburg/Marktplatz.note: Late-Gothic town hall and burgher houses.

naumburg/St Wenceslas.name: St Wenceslas
naumburg/St Wenceslas.note: Has a Hildebrandt organ that Bach himself tested in 1746.

naumburg/Saale-Unstrut wine.name: Saale-Unstrut wine
naumburg/Saale-Unstrut wine.note: The northernmost quality wine region in Europe.

quedlinburg/Old town.name: Old town
quedlinburg/Old town.note: UNESCO. Around 1300 half-timbered houses from six centuries.
quedlinburg/Old town.photoFile: Quedlinburg asv2018-10 img04 pano from Muenzenberg.jpg

quedlinburg/Schlossberg and collegiate c.name: Schlossberg and collegiate church
quedlinburg/Schlossberg and collegiate c.note: Romanesque church on the castle rock, with the Ottonian treasury.

quedlinburg/Marktplatz.name: Marktplatz
quedlinburg/Marktplatz.note: Renaissance town hall with a Roland statue in front.

quedlinburg/Finkenherd.name: Finkenherd
quedlinburg/Finkenherd.note: The oldest corner of town, below the castle rock.

quedlinburg/Half-timbered museum.name: Half-timbered museum
quedlinburg/Half-timbered museum.note: In a house from about 1310 — one of the oldest in Germany.

magdeburg/Magdeburg Cathedral.name: Magdeburg Cathedral
magdeburg/Magdeburg Cathedral.note: The first Gothic cathedral on German soil, on the Elbe.

magdeburg/Green Citadel.name: Green Citadel
magdeburg/Green Citadel.note: Hundertwasser's last building. Pink, wonky, full of trees.

magdeburg/Elbe promenade.name: Elbe promenade
magdeburg/Elbe promenade.note: River walk between the cathedral and the bridges.

magdeburg/Monastery of Our Lady.name: Monastery of Our Lady
magdeburg/Monastery of Our Lady.note: Romanesque monastery, now a sculpture museum.

berlin/Brandenburg Gate.name: Brandenburg Gate
berlin/Brandenburg Gate.note: The obvious one, and still worth standing in front of.

berlin/Gendarmenmarkt.name: Gendarmenmarkt
berlin/Gendarmenmarkt.note: Two matching cathedrals and the concert hall. The handsomest square in Berlin.

berlin/Museum Island.name: Museum Island
berlin/Museum Island.note: Five museums on one island. The Pergamon's Ishtar Gate is the highlight.
berlin/Museum Island.about: The Museum Island is a museum complex on the northern part of Spree Island in the historic heart of Berlin, Germany. It is one of the capital's most visited sights and one of the most important museum sites in Europe.

berlin/Reichstag dome.name: Reichstag dome
berlin/Reichstag dome.note: Free, but you must register online in advance.

berlin/Berlin Cathedral.name: Berlin Cathedral
berlin/Berlin Cathedral.note: Climb to the dome walkway for the view over the island.

berlin/Memorial to the Murdered Jews of.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
berlin/Memorial to the Murdered Jews of.note: 2711 concrete slabs. Walk into the middle of it.

berlin/Tiergarten.name: Tiergarten
berlin/Tiergarten.note: The big central park, with the Victory Column in the middle.

berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.name: Alexanderplatz TV Tower
berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.note: 368 m. Book a time slot to skip the queue.
berlin/Alexanderplatz TV Tower.about: The Fernsehturm in central Berlin was constructed between 1965 and 1969 by the government of the German Democratic Republic as both a functional broadcasting facility and a symbol of communist power.

berlin/Checkpoint Charlie.name: Checkpoint Charlie
berlin/Checkpoint Charlie.note: The old crossing point. Busy and a bit tacky, but it is the spot.

berlin/Charlottenburg Palace.name: Charlottenburg Palace
berlin/Charlottenburg Palace.note: The largest palace in Berlin, with a big park behind it.

berlin/Hackesche Höfe.name: Hackesche Höfe
berlin/Hackesche Höfe.note: Eight linked courtyards of shops and cafés in Mitte.
